title: Mixedness passes to subobjects, quotients, extensions and direct summands
statement:
Fix $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$ and $w\in\mathbf R$, and let
$Y_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme. In the abelian category of
constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaves on $Y_0$
([def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], [def-weil-constructible-heart]):

1. every Weil subsheaf and every Weil quotient sheaf of a sheaf that is
   $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$ in the sense of
   [def-weil-punctual-weights] is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$;
2. if $0\to\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G\to\mathcal G''\to0$ is an exact
   sequence of constructible Weil sheaves and $\mathcal G'$,
   $\mathcal G''$ are $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$, then so is
   $\mathcal G$;
3. in particular, a direct summand of an $\iota$-mixed constructible
   Weil sheaf of weights at most $w$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most
   $w$.

The analogous statements hold for Frobenius modules in the sense of
[def-weil-frobenius-module-weights].

proof.text: The sheaf assertions are already supplied by AlgebraicGeometry.WeilSheaf.IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost.of_mono, of_epi, of_shortExact and of_retract in the publicly imported WeilConjectures.DeligneLaumon.Reduction.Weights. This delivery proves the remaining finite-filtration Frobenius-module analogue without changing those imported assertions.

For a mixed Frobenius module as in [def-weil-frobenius-module-weights], prove the eigenvalue upper bound by induction along its finite filtration. Given a nonzero eigenvector in V_(j+1), either it lies in V_j and induction applies, or its class in V_(j+1)/V_j is nonzero. The defining induced-action equation makes that class an eigenvector with the same eigenvalue. Purity of this graded piece gives its modulus q^(w_j/2), which is at most q^(w/2) since q=p^a >= 1. The base case is V_0=0. This is the fully proved private helper mixed_eigenvalue_bound; no characteristic-polynomial factorization is required.

For an injective equivariant map A -> B, map an eigenvector of A into B. Injectivity keeps it nonzero, and equivariance and linearity preserve its eigenvalue. Apply the preceding bound for mixed B, then [lem-a1-punctual-bound-module-mixed] to A. For a surjective equivariant map A -> B, use the proved library theorem FrobeniusModule.hasEigenvalue_of_hasEigenvector_mem_range: every eigenvector of B is in the range, so its eigenvalue occurs on A. Apply the bound for mixed A and the same filtered criterion to B. This theorem is universe-polymorphic for the independently sized carriers in the statement.

Apply [lem-a1-extension-bounds] directly with the given equivariant maps, injectivity, function exactness, surjectivity and mixed outer terms. This is precisely FrobeniusModule.IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost.of_shortExact, with the same independent carrier universes and parameters.

A linear retraction r comp i = id gives r(i(x))=x for every x, hence i is injective. Apply the injective-map assertion proved above to the split inclusion. The proof does not need equivariance of r, although that original hypothesis is preserved.

proof_origin.place: Final Frobenius-module paragraph; finite-filtration eigenvector induction and existing punctual-bound criterion replace the canonical-subquotient presentation.

lean.statement: theorem mixedOfWeightsAtMost_stability (p a ell : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (ha : 1 ≤ a) [Fact ell.Prime] (hellp : ell ≠ p) (Qlb : Type v) [Field Qlb] [Algebra ℚ_[ell] Qlb] (hQ : IsAlgClosure ℚ_[ell] Qlb) (iota : Qlb ≃+* ℂ) (w : ℝ) : (∀ (A : FrobeniusModule.{u₁, v} Qlb) (B : FrobeniusModule.{u₂, v} Qlb) (f : A.carrier →ₗ[Qlb] B.carrier), (∀ x : A.carrier, f (A.frobenius x) = B.frobenius (f x)) → Function.Injective f → IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost p a ell ha hellp Qlb hQ iota B w → IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost p a ell ha hellp Qlb hQ iota A w) ∧ (∀ (A : FrobeniusModule.{u₁, v} Qlb) (B : FrobeniusModule.{u₂, v} Qlb) (g : A.carrier →ₗ[Qlb] B.carrier), (∀ x : A.carrier, g (A.frobenius x) = B.frobenius (g x)) → Function.Surjective g → IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost p a ell ha hellp Qlb hQ iota A w → IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost p a ell ha hellp Qlb hQ iota B w) ∧ (∀ (A : FrobeniusModule.{u₁, v} Qlb) (B : FrobeniusModule.{u₂, v} Qlb) (C : FrobeniusModule.{u₃, v} Qlb) (f : A.carrier →ₗ[Qlb] B.carrier) (g : B.carrier →ₗ[Qlb] C.carrier), (∀ x : A.carrier, f (A.frobenius x) = B.frobenius (f x)) → (∀ x : B.carrier, g (B.frobenius x) = C.frobenius (g x)) → Function.Injective f → Function.Exact f g → Function.Surjective g → IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost p a ell ha hellp Qlb hQ iota A w → IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost p a ell ha hellp Qlb hQ iota C w → IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost p a ell ha hellp Qlb hQ iota B w) ∧ (∀ (A : FrobeniusModule.{u₁, v} Qlb) (B : FrobeniusModule.{u₂, v} Qlb) (i : A.carrier →ₗ[Qlb] B.carrier) (r : B.carrier →ₗ[Qlb] A.carrier), (∀ x : A.carrier, i (A.frobenius x) = B.frobenius (i x)) → (∀ x : B.carrier, r (B.frobenius x) = A.frobenius (r x)) → r.comp i = LinearMap.id → IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost p a ell ha hellp Qlb hQ iota B w → IsMixedOfWeightsAtMost p a ell ha hellp Qlb hQ iota A w)
lean.note: Mixed record: all four sheaf clauses are exact existing declarations in the live upstream recorded punctual-weight module. The new theorem supplies all four analogues for the current finite stable-filtration Frobenius-module predicate. The sheaf clauses use the concrete constructible pro-etale Weil-sheaf category required by the recorded punctual-weight declaration, not the upstream derived category of Weil sheaves.
